To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
uncertainty orientation and control deprivation interact to affect information processing in moderately depressed persons.

moderately depressed people who are uncertainty-oriented increase information seeking when they are control deprived, whereas moderately depressed people who have a certainty orientation decrease information seeking when they feel deprived of control.

moderately depressed persons who are uncertainty oriented are likely to seek information about the source of their control deprivation, whereas moderately depressed certainty-oriented persons are not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between uncertainty orientation and control deprivation in moderate depressives.
the role that information processing plays in the self-regulatory process.
the relationship between depression, information processing, and uncertainty orientation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of the two studies are consistent with the hypothesis that uncertainty-oriented moderately depressed persons are more likely than certainty-oriented moderately depressed persons to seek information when control is threatened.
moderately depressed persons, when they are uncertainty oriented, will increase information processing when control deprived, but only when they have a high desire for control.
uncertainty orientation moderates the relationship between control motivation and information processing in moderately depressed persons, but does not do so in nondepressed persons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
uncertainty-orientation moderates depression's effect on information-processing, and that the effects are different depending on whether the task is performance or informational.
uncertainty orientation is an important individual-difference variable that interacts with depression in the processing of information about control.

uncertainty-oriented persons are more likely to seek information when control deprived and that moderately depressed persons are more likely than non-depressed persons to seek information when deprived of control.
The main takeaway from our work is that
depression may be related to information processing in ways that differ from the information processing that has been studied in the context of uncertainty orientation.
depression is a complex phenomenon that can be better understood by taking an individual differences approach.
depression is not a unitary construct, and that it is important to understand the specific ways in which depression manifests itself.
